_comment: Every answer POST /v1/sessions/summarize gives, and what the client's outbox does with each.
Read by both ends of the response, and by neither's production code: the request has
summarize-request.v1.json, and this is its other half. The backend's SummarizeResponse writes these
bodies; the client's DraftSender reads them. Nothing else binds the two, and a rename on either side
used to turn every 200 into a body the client could not read, which it retried, billed, until the
outbox gave up, with no note at the end of it (2026-10-12 review).
Each outcome has its own HTTP status, and the status decides: `status` in the body is for a person.
`client` is what the outbox is told. done stores the draft. retry queues it and asks again later,
and waits at least `retry_after_seconds` when the backend sent a Retry-After. failed tells the
technician, because asking again would get the same answer at the same price.
busy is the endpoint refusing a device or tenant already drafting as many sessions as it may at
once. It is answered before the bundle is read.
Change this file only when both sides change with it. EachOutcomeReachesTheClientAsItsOwnStatus
(backend) and EachOutcomeIsWhatTheOutboxIsTold (client) are the pair that notice. The ok draft is
written against summarize-request.v1.json's session, so the backend's rules accept it.
